summary: Christoph Anderl is a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an MA at the University of Vienna (~1989–1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier (~1997–2004).

Christoph Cüppers works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1973–1983) under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1994–2013).

Christoph Emmrich specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels (~1999–2004), holding a post there (~2003–2006) before serving as Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto (~2006–2012).

Christoph Harbsmeier specializes in sinology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford and earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen. He became a professor at the University of Oslo (~1985) and held advisory professorships in China.

Christoph Kleine works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, completing his Habilitation at the University of Marburg (-2001). He was a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (2004–2008) and Leipzig University (~2008).

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Professor at SOAS University of London (~1950–1976) and held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (~1951–1976).
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He has held positions as professeur at Université catholique de Louvain (~1999) and professeur de sanskrit at KU Leuven.

Christopher André Holmboe was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo (1810) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval. He was Professor of Oriental Languages at Oslo (1818–1828).

Christopher Byrne specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at McGill University, completing an MA under G. Victor Sōgen Hori (-2009) and a PhD under Grace S. Fong (~2009–2015), also studying under Robin D. S. Yates.

Christopher D. Emms is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at McMaster University (~2010–2012) under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke and committee members James A. Benn and Mark Rowe.

Christopher D. Wallis works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley for his PhD under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt (~2006–2014). He served as a guest lecturer at Naropa University.

Christopher Framarin specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii (~1999–2001) and a PhD at the University of New Mexico (~2001–2005), becoming associate professor at the University of Calgary (~2006).

Christopher Hatchell specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) with David Germano as academic mentor, and also studied under Trinley Nyima Rinpoche.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Ohio State University and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, becoming a professor at Indiana University in 1982.

Christopher Ives is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2001).

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, where he completed his PhD (~2011–2018) under James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2001–2011). He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held posts at Stony Brook University and the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (~1980–1985), and became Doshi Professor at Loyola Marymount University (~1985).

Christopher Minkowski is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Harvard. He held posts at Iowa, Brown, and Cornell (~1992–2005), and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (~2005–2023).
Christopher Pinney is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He has held academic posts at the Australian National University, the University of Chicago, and University College London (~1994).
